title: Git + GitHub
summary: Version control from the ground up: status, staging, commits, branches, remotes, forks, and pushing and pulling with GitHub. You already use these through /save-project; this lecture explains what each command does. The step-by-step arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Explain and run the git workflow (status → add → commit → push/pull) and create, switch and merge branches without Claude's help.

steps.title: Read the two curriculum lessons
steps.detail: Skim Git Fundamentals and GitHub Fundamentals. Focus on staging vs committing, branches, and linking a local repo to a remote. This sets up the main / dev / feature branches from AI-10 DevOps.
steps.doneWhen: You can say in one sentence each what git add, git commit, git push and git pull do.

steps.title: Try Learn Git Branching 1–3
steps.detail: The curriculum lists Learn Git Branching, Introduction Sequence levels 1–3. It's a free browser game that draws your branches as you type.
steps.doneWhen: Introduction Sequence levels 1–3 show as solved.

steps.title: Look at your own repo's history
steps.detail: Run these in ~/Desktop/codeplatoon/assignments/week-02/netflix to see the commits and branches you already made, and which remote they push to.
steps.code:
git log --oneline --graph --all | head -20
git branch -a
git remote -v
steps.doneWhen: You can point to your latest commit, your branches, and the origin URL.

steps.title: Note the listed assignments
steps.detail: The curriculum page lists: Git Practice, Learn Git Branching (Introduction 1–3), GitHub Practice, and a stretch Git Group Project. Wait for Slack to confirm which ones Eagle gets before forking.
steps.doneWhen: You know which repos to expect; start them with /start-assignment once they're posted.

concepts.meaning: A folder whose history git tracks.
The list of changes you've picked (git add) for the next commit.
A saved snapshot of the staged changes, with a message.
A separate line of commits, so you can work without touching main.
The copy of the repo on GitHub; origin is its default name.
Your own GitHub copy of someone else's repo (how you get assignments).
